Hi again,

as you correctly pointed out this is a regression caused by #12425 
I'm assuming you are following the guide here https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/dialects/mysql.html#rendering-on-update-current-timestamp-for-mysql-mariadb-s-explicit-defaults-for-timestamp

The simplest workaround seems to be to use uppercase for ON UPDATE. Can you test it?
I guess the fix should be make the check for `on update` case insensitive

Hi @CaselIT ,
I can confirm that it works with uppercase.

Should I create a PR to make the check case insensitive?
it would be great. It's likely enough to just add a casefold where it does the check and add a test that is lowercase

issue.title: Use lower case on update in server_defaults #12488
issue.body:
This fixes a bug where using lowercase for `on update` in the server_defaults would generate incorrect DDL.

### Description
Fixes #12488

issue.title: more mysql server default parenthesization rules are needed to know to not render parenthesis for a function that is exactly NOW/CURRENT_TIMESTAMP with fractional seconds

labels.name: regression
labels.description: something worked and was broken by a change

issue.body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/discussions/12646
Originally posted by **YamaguchiTsubasaA** June 5, 2025 #### Describe the bug In SQLAlchemy version 2.0.40 and later, using `server_default=sa.text('CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3)')` results in the default value of the created column being set to `now(3)` instead of `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3)`. This issue is similar to the one reported in [#12488](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/12488), which was supposed to be resolved in version 2.0.41. However, this particular problem has not been fixed. I am using Alembic code in the reproduction steps mentioned below, but I believe this is a problem with SQLAlchemy, not Alembic. #### Expected behavior When executing `show create table sample table;` , I would like the result to look like the following (this is how tables have been created up to v2.0.039): ```sql CREATE TABLE `sample_table` ( `id` varchar(100) COLLATE utf8mb4_bin NOT NULL, `val` varchar(100) COLLATE utf8mb4_bin NOT NULL, `created_at` datetime(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3), `updated_at` datetime(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3) ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3), PRIMARY KEY (`id`) ) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_bin ``` #### Error But here’s what it actually looks like: ```sql CREATE TABLE `sample_table` ( `id` varchar(100) COLLATE utf8mb4_bin NOT NULL, `val` varchar(100) COLLATE utf8mb4_bin NOT NULL, `created_at` datetime(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT (now(3)), `updated_at` datetime(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3) ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3), PRIMARY KEY (`id`) ) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_bin ``` #### To Reproduce models.py ```python from datetime import datetime from sqlalchemy import text from sqlalchemy.dialects.mysql import DATETIME from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column from sqlalchemy.schema import PrimaryKeyConstraint from sqlalchemy.types import String class SampleModelBase(DeclarativeBase): pass class SampleTable(SampleModelBase): __tablename__ = "sample_table" __table_args__ = ( PrimaryKeyConstraint("id", name="pk_key"), ) id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(100)) val: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(100)) created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column( DATETIME(fsp=3), server_default=text("CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3)")) updated_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column( DATETIME(fsp=3), server_default=text( "CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3) ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3)")) ``` Creating a revision in Alembic. ```python """create_sample_table Revision ID: 13ad61307f3f Revises: 05c21f732e0e Create Date: 2025-06-04 17:31:55.870252 """ import sqlalchemy as sa from alembic import op from sqlalchemy.dialects import mysql # revision identifiers, used by Alembic. revision = "13ad61307f3f" down_revision = None branch_labels = None depends_on = None def upgrade() -> None: # ### commands auto generated by Alembic - please adjust! ### op.create_table("sample_table", sa.Column("id", sa.String(length=100), nullable=False), sa.Column("val", sa.String(length=100), nullable=False), sa.Column("created_at", mysql.DATETIME(fsp=3), server_default=sa.text("CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3)"), nullable=False), sa.Column("updated_at", mysql.DATETIME(fsp=3), server_default=sa.text("CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3) ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3)"), nullable=False), sa.PrimaryKeyConstraint("id", name="pk_key") ) # ### end Alembic commands ### def downgrade() -> None: # ### commands auto generated by Alembic - please adjust! ### op.drop_table("sample_table") # ### end Alembic commands ### ``` When executing `show create table sample_table;` for the above revision, the result looks like this: ```sql CREATE TABLE `sample_table` ( `id` varchar(100) COLLATE utf8mb4_bin NOT NULL, `val` varchar(100) COLLATE utf8mb4_bin NOT NULL, `created_at` datetime(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT (now(3)), `updated_at` datetime(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3) ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3), PRIMARY KEY (`id`) ) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_bin ``` #### Supplementary Information After the reproduction procedure, without changing the model definition, when the revision file was created again, an alter_column operation was generated. ```python """create_sample_table no change model Revision ID: b80f26ce31c6 Revises: 13ad61307f3f Create Date: 2025-06-04 18:14:55.977744 """ from alembic import op import sqlalchemy as sa from sqlalchemy.dialects import mysql # revision identifiers, used by Alembic. revision = 'b80f26ce31c6' down_revision = '13ad61307f3f' branch_labels = None depends_on = None def upgrade() -> None: # ### commands auto generated by Alembic - please adjust! ### op.alter_column('sample_table', 'created_at', existing_type=mysql.DATETIME(fsp=3), server_default=sa.text('CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3)'), existing_nullable=False) # ### end Alembic commands ### def downgrade() -> None: # ### commands auto generated by Alembic - please adjust! ### op.alter_column('sample_table', 'created_at', existing_type=mysql.DATETIME(fsp=3), server_default=sa.text('(now(3))'), existing_nullable=False) # ### end Alembic commands ### ``` When executing `show create table sample_table;` for the table modified by the above ```sql CREATE TABLE `sample_table` ( `id` varchar(100) COLLATE utf8mb4_bin NOT NULL, `val` varchar(100) COLLATE utf8mb4_bin NOT NULL, `created_at` datetime(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3), `updated_at` datetime(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3) ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3), PRIMARY KEY (`id`) ) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_bin ``` While `create_table` results in `now(3)`, it seems that `alter_column` sets it to `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(3)`. #### Versions: - OS: ubuntu 22.04 - Python: 3.10.3 - Alembic: 1.16.1 - SQLAlchemy: 2.0.39 / 2.0.41 - Database: MySQL 8.0.35 - DBAPI: mysql-connector-python 9.3.0
